tasks.title: Verify the daimon accepts a loopback http:// URL (OQ-A)
tasks.detail: No vendor package uses a local http:// url — all three are remote HTTPS. Emit a single-server manifest pointing at http://localhost:8942/mcp, restart Kimi Desktop, and confirm the tool appears. If loopback is refused, STOP: record the change as inert and do not ship a manifest field that cannot work.
tasks.verify: Kimi Desktop lists a prometheus-knowledge tool, or a recorded refusal

tasks.title: Determine whether the url form drives surreal-memory's legacy SSE transport
tasks.detail: surreal-memory answers GET /mcp/sse with an `event: endpoint` pointing at /mcp/messages?sessionId=... — a two-channel session transport. No vendor example exercises this. If the daimon cannot drive it, omit the server and record why.
tasks.verify: surreal-memory tools appear in Kimi Desktop, or an omission comment citing the probe

tasks.title: Emit mcpServers from the generator
tasks.detail: Add the mcpServers object to the manifest dict in the Python heredoc of install-kimi-desktop-plugin.sh. Include prometheus-knowledge; include surreal-memory only per t2; exclude forge-rs with a comment citing the 401 and the missing auth-header field.
tasks.verify: generated kimi.plugin.json contains the expected mcpServers keys

tasks.title: Resolve port hardcoding (OQ-B)
tasks.detail: Ports 23001/8942 are embedded. Check whether they are user-configurable in the pack's own config; if so, read the value at generation time rather than hardcoding, so a reinstall on a machine with different ports still works (goal 4).
tasks.verify: either ports are read from config, or a comment records that they are fixed by contract

tasks.title: Regression: idempotence and payload
tasks.detail: Delete the installed package, re-run install-skills-flat.sh, confirm restoration with 145 skills and no binary inside the package.
tasks.verify: 145 skills present; find <pkg> -type f -perm +111 returns no Mach-O
